column1: # Source suffix | Revised distractor 1 | Revised distractor 2 | Explanation | Editorial note | Teacher flag | Neutral hint override | Context override

001|Volunteers joined in surprisingly large numbers, but not necessarily quickly.|Volunteer numbers fluctuated unpredictably.|At an astonishing rate describes a surprising speed of change. Here it is the speed of recruitment, not just the final number of volunteers.|Distinguish rate from total and variation.|none||

002|The lake was already polluted when observations began.|The pollution level rose and fell with no overall direction.|Increasingly shows a growing degree over time. It does not simply say that pollution was already present.|Separate a trend from an initial condition.|none||

003|People were kept out of the lanes by a formal closure.|People were spread evenly through the available lanes.|Congested describes a space so crowded that movement is difficult. The lanes need not be officially closed.|Movement restriction versus administrative closure.|none||

004|It planned to replace old equipment within the same space.|It planned to combine existing facilities under one manager.|An expansion increases size or capacity. Replacement or reorganisation alone would not necessarily make the facilities larger.|Size/capacity distinguished from replacement.|none||

005|The trains would travel underground in shallow tunnels.|The trains would connect outer suburbs without specifying track height.|Overground means above the ground surface. It describes where the line runs, not which districts it connects.|Avoid a bus-versus-rail giveaway; review British railway terminology.|terminology: generic overground, not a branded operator||

006|Separate paths served each village without joining one another.|A single main path passed each village in turn.|A network is a system of connected parts. The emphasis is on linked paths, rather than one isolated route.|Connected system versus single route.|none||

007|Expensive repairs might be the reason maintenance is skipped.|Skipping maintenance might occur alongside repairs, without causing them.|Result in introduces a consequence. Skipping maintenance is the cause in this sentence; the repairs are the possible result.|Test causal direction, not unrelated vocabulary.|none||

008|Each employee working on board needed a ticket.|Each person waiting to collect an arriving traveller needed a ticket.|A passenger travels in a vehicle without being its driver or crew. A person waiting to meet someone is not necessarily a passenger.|Traveller versus crew or greeter.|none||

009|It travelled to the country's largest commercial city, whether or not it was the seat of government.|It travelled to the region where the delegation's funding was held.|Capital here is the city serving as a country's seat of government. It is not automatically the biggest city, and it is not the money sense of capital.|Retain source city sense; avoid equating capital with largest city.|polysemy: main city definition should be read as seat of government||

011|It was a moment remembered only because it happened a long time ago.|It was a routine event recorded in historical documents.|Historic stresses importance in history. Merely being old or recorded in the past does not make an event historic.|Distinguish historic from historical.|none||

012|They arranged themselves in two parallel rows.|They gathered in a close group on one side.|Form a ring means arrange people or objects in a circle. Standing around the performer supplies the spatial context.|Use plausible audience arrangements.|none||

013|The six instruments were optional additions to the toolkit.|The toolkit was designed to produce six instruments.|Consist of introduces the parts that make up a whole. The instruments are its components, not optional extras or its products.|Part/whole relationship and consist of structure.|none||

014|The shed was well made but had not been maintained for many years.|The shed was unfinished, without any claim about construction quality.|Poorly modifies built: the standard of construction was low. Its first storm rules out years of wear as the main explanation.|Quality versus age and completion.|none||

015|The room was busy but still comfortably accommodated everyone.|People waited a long time because appointments were running late.|Overcrowded means too many people for the available space. A room can be busy, or waits can be long, without being overcrowded.|Retain teacher-approved context and answer-neutral people/space clue.|none||

016|It examined a densely populated city area with adequate, well-maintained housing.|It examined a low-income rural settlement outside the city.|In this source sense, slum refers to an urban area with poor, overcrowded housing conditions. Density or low income alone is not a complete definition.|Preserve Supporting priority; describe housing conditions without labelling residents.|sensitive terminology: teacher should confirm classroom wording||

017|The horse accompanied the cart but did not pull it.|People pushed the cart while horses carried visitors separately.|The compound horse-drawn identifies the pulling force: a horse draws the vehicle. It does not merely describe a horse nearby.|Physical role of drawn in a compound adjective.|none||

018|The journey was worrying beforehand but went smoothly.|The journey was a frightening dream rather than a real experience.|A nightmare can figuratively mean a very difficult or unpleasant experience. Here it describes the real disrupted journey, not sleep.|Figurative sense versus literal dream.|none||

019|They left them in a luggage room on the station platform.|They left them in the separate engine compartment.|In a railway setting, carriage means a passenger coach or compartment. The station and the locomotive are different parts of the journey.|Clarify train sense within workbook's broader carriage entry.|polysemy: workbook combines train coach and horse-drawn vehicle||

020|Residents attended repeatedly over several days.|Residents from many different backgrounds attended, regardless of number.|Numerous tells us there were many residents. It says nothing by itself about repeated attendance or the group's diversity.|Quantity versus frequency/diversity.|none||

021|It announced a timetable of lighting inspection dates only.|It reported a completed improvement rather than an organised plan.|In this British-English context, a scheme is an organised plan or programme. It does not have to mean a dishonest plot.|Replace absurd distractors; flag regional connotation.|regional sense: neutral British-English scheme||

022|They will formally approve a crossing that has already been suggested.|They will build the crossing before any decision is made.|Propose means put an idea forward for consideration. Suggesting a crossing is different from approving or building it.|Contrast suggestion, authorisation and execution.|none||

023|It should postpone dealing with the conflict.|It should identify the conflict without fixing it.|Resolve means find a solution so the problem is settled. Identifying or delaying a conflict is not the same as resolving it.|Problem-solving stages as distractors.|none||

024|The team hoped merely to take part, regardless of the result.|The team hoped to finish preparing, whether or not the project worked.|Succeed means achieve the intended result, not simply take part or finish preparation. A common pattern is succeed in doing something.|Replace awkward It/team reference and answer-echo explanation.|none||

025|She privately agreed but avoided expressing a public view.|She publicly described the safety debate without taking sides.|A vocal advocate openly and actively supports a cause. Reporting both sides neutrally is different from advocating one side.|Public support versus private agreement/reporting.|none||

026|The buyer sought a surveyor's assessment of the building's physical condition.|The buyer sought an estate agent's help marketing the property.|A solicitor is a legal practitioner who can handle a property's legal paperwork. Surveying its condition and marketing it are different professional roles.|Plausible property professionals rather than builder/reporter.|jurisdiction: source sense is England and Wales||

027|It described benefits only for investors, without wider community effects.|It described social popularity without any financial or economic effects.|Social advantages benefit people or communities; economic advantages concern resources, employment or money. The phrase includes both kinds of benefit.|Require both parts of the phrase.|none||

028|It will make the two trails similar without joining them.|It will improve one trail while leaving the other separate.|Link together stresses a connection between previously separate things. Similarity or improvement alone does not create that connection.|Relationship rather than general improvement.|none||

029|It aimed only to clean streets while leaving the housing in place.|It aimed to renovate existing housing without removing it.|Clear slums in this source means remove poor-quality housing areas for redevelopment. Clear here is not ordinary street cleaning; it also does not itself mean renovation.|Avoid implying a social benefit or residents' consent from clearance alone.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|sensitive redevelopment terminology and social impact|Focus on what redevelopment would do to the housing, rather than to the street surface.|

030|It will change its internal layout at the same address.|It will extend its opening hours at its current site.|Relocate means move to a different location. A studio can reorganise its rooms or hours without relocating.|Location versus internal changes.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Look at what 'to another district' contributes to the sentence.|

031|It opened a centre in an outer residential suburb.|It opened a centre serving urban families from a rural site.|Inner-city locates something in or near the city's central urban area. It describes location, not merely the people a service supports.|Location rather than audience.|none||

032|The bridge had recently been repaired but was originally built long ago.|The bridge had recently received approval but building had not begun.|Newly constructed means recently built. Recent repairs or planning approval are not equivalent to new construction.|Repair and approval are plausible near misses.|none||

033|It moved to the central business district.|It moved to an independent rural village with no urban connection.|A suburb is a residential area on the outskirts of a town or city. It belongs to the wider urban area even though it is outside the busy centre.|Geographical relation to centre.|none||

034|It will recommend helmets but leave participants to obtain their own.|It will check helmets that participants already own.|Provide means make something available or supply it. Advice and inspection alone would not supply helmets.|Supply versus recommend/check.|none||

035|The campaign became more widely known without gaining approval.|Supporters began to withdraw their backing.|Gain support means attract more approval or backing. Public awareness alone can grow even when people do not support a campaign.|Approval versus awareness.|none||

036|The architect must privately draft a plan without sending it for approval.|The architect must receive final permission for a plan already submitted.|Submit a plan means present it officially to be considered. Drafting precedes submission; approval is a later decision.|Process sequence and collocation.|none||

037|It accepted the application subject to further conditions.|It postponed a decision without accepting or refusing it.|Reject means refuse to accept or approve. A delayed decision or conditional acceptance is different from rejection.|Refusal versus delay/conditional approval.|none||

038|The festival will be planned by the same people as the holidays.|The festival will take place immediately after the holidays finish.|Coincide with expresses shared timing. Events can coincide without having the same organisers or causing one another.|Time relation, not personnel or sequence.|none||

039|It discussed the final construction contract for an already approved garden.|It inspected a garden already completed under the plan.|A proposal is a suggested plan for consideration. It is not the completed project or necessarily the final legal agreement.|Plan versus implementation/contract.|none||

040|It agreed to discuss the proposal but withheld approval.|It passed the documents to another committee without deciding.|Pass a proposal here means approve it formally. The context is a council vote, not physically handing over a document.|Procedural approval versus transmission.|none||

041|They agreed to cooperate while remaining separate organisations.|They agreed to divide one organisation into two.|Merge means combine into a single entity. Cooperation can happen without a merger, while division moves in the opposite direction.|Merger versus collaboration and split.|none||

042|They hope to move into an existing centre without founding one.|They hope to make an existing centre better known.|Establish a centre means formally set it up. Publicising or occupying an existing centre does not necessarily establish a new one.|Founding versus promotion/occupation.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Focus on what the graduates hope to do, rather than which building they will occupy.|

043|They will design a shelter without building it yet.|They will inspect a shelter that has already been built.|Construct means build. Designing and inspecting are related activities, but neither alone means construction.|Physical building versus adjacent tasks.|none||

044|It tried to estimate how much money the roof would cost.|It tried to allocate money that it already had.|Raise funding means secure money for a project. Estimating a cost or allocating existing funds is a different step.|Financing versus budgeting.|none||

045|The redesign made a few routine improvements to the old layout.|The redesign restored the traditional layout as closely as possible.|Radical describes a fundamental departure from conventional ideas. Minor adjustments or a faithful restoration are not radical redesigns.|Degree of change within architecture.|none||

046|The views were a minor reason compared with every other feature.|The views were the only possible reason for its popularity.|Not least because of emphasises an important reason. It does not mean that reason was unimportant or the only reason.|Emphasis without unsupported exclusivity.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|How does the phrase before because guide your reading of the reason that follows?|

047|It said wheelchair access was essential but expressed no disapproval.|It praised the access arrangements while listing their features.|Critical of means expressing disapproval or pointing out faults. Critical meaning essential is a different sense, not the sense in this review.|Intended evaluative sense of critical of.|polysemy: distinguish critical of from critical to||

048|Only the organisation's own publicity staff paid attention.|Only the people who printed the announcement's leaflets paid attention.|The press means news media collectively, such as newspapers and reporters. It is not simply a company's publicity team or printing staff.|Same topic, different communication roles.|none||

049|A person asking for clarification without taking a position spoke.|A person supporting the plan offered suggestions for improvement.|An objector opposes a proposal. Asking a neutral question, or supporting a plan while improving it, does not by itself make someone an objector.|Opposition versus neutral enquiry/qualified support.|none||

050|They quote a view without endorsing it or giving reasons.|They present the view as an agreed fact requiring no support.|Argue that introduces a reasoned position or claim. Academic argue need not imply an angry disagreement or physical confrontation.|Academic reporting verb, evidence versus quotation.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Read the clause after that. What kind of statement are the researchers making?|

051|It could develop small surface cracks while remaining standing.|It could bend slightly and then return to its original position.|Collapse means lose structural support and fall down. Minor cracking or temporary bending need not involve collapse.|Failure versus less severe damage.|none||

052|They checked cables at the same height along the wall.|They checked the extra operating costs of the cable system.|Overhead locates the cables above the workers. The cost sense of overheads is not intended in this physical setting.|Source physical sense; preserve alternative cost as plausible distractor.|none||

053|The windows moved slowly into a permanently different position.|The windows stayed still while nearby walls vibrated.|Shake means move rapidly back and forth. A single slow shift, or vibration elsewhere, is not what the sentence says.|Movement type and grammatical subject.|none||

054|It could alter the pond's appearance without harming the fish.|It could move fish away through an unpleasant smell without toxic harm.|Poison means harm through a toxic substance. An unpleasant appearance or smell alone does not establish poisoning.|Toxic harm without adding unsupported mechanism.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Consider why a chemical leak would be a concern for the pond.|

055|It aimed to capture smoke after it had already spread through the surrounding neighbourhood.|It aimed to reduce smoke produced indoors without changing what was released outside.|Emissions are substances released from a source into the environment. Filters target what leaves the factory, rather than merely changing indoor conditions.|Released substances versus indoor production/cleanup.|none||

056|They repeated an activity only after every obstacle had disappeared.|They stopped experimenting when the first trial failed.|Persist emphasises continuing despite difficulty or opposition. The failed trials make that persistence significant.|Continuation despite obstacles rather than mere repetition.|none||

057|It will encourage users to visit without changing physical access.|It will require every visitor to use a wheelchair.|Enable someone to do something means make it possible. Encouragement alone is different from removing a physical barrier.|Possibility versus encouragement/obligation.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|What difference would the ramp make compared with a stage reached only by steps?|

058|It borrowed equipment without putting money into it.|It calculated equipment costs but made no financial commitment.|Invest in means commit money or resources for an expected benefit. Calculating costs does not itself mean investing.|Commitment versus estimate or loan of equipment.|none||

059|It reopened immediately, without any period of repairs.|It reopened at regular intervals throughout the repairs.|Eventually places an event at the end of a period, often after delay. It is not the same as immediately or repeatedly.|End of a sequence versus frequency.|none||

060|The driver checked the distance only, without considering the path.|The driver checked a list of departure times.|A route is the course taken from one place to another. Distance and timetable information can accompany a route but are not the route itself.|Path versus measurement/schedule.|none||

061|It is beside the hall on the same floor.|It is above the hall, within the roof space.|Beneath means underneath, describing a lower position. It does not simply mean nearby.|Vertical position relative to a reference.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Compare the positions of the chamber and the hall.|

062|They help keep waste at its present level.|They make the waste easier to collect without reducing its amount.|Minimise means make an amount as small as possible. Handling waste more easily does not necessarily reduce it.|Reduction versus management or stability.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Compare the amount of packaging left after using the containers.|

063|The extra income from the repairs caused difficulty.|The extra workload caused difficulty without any added financial cost.|Expense is money spent or a cost incurred. In this sentence, afford signals the financial sense.|Cost versus workload and income.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|What does difficult to afford tell you about the kind of burden being discussed?|

064|They could renovate it while preserving the structure.|They could dismantle and move it intact for reuse elsewhere.|Demolish means deliberately destroy a structure by tearing it down. Repairing or relocating an intact building is different.|Destruction versus renovation/relocation.|none||

065|Friday was the date finally chosen after the Sunday plan changed.|Friday was the actual performance date, regardless of the original plan.|Originally scheduled identifies the first planned time. The later move to Sunday changes the schedule, not the original intention.|Initial, final and actual dates distinguished.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Trace the two dates in the order in which the plans were made.|

066|Design work began, but no building activity had started.|Medical services began in an already completed centre.|Construction is the process of building. Designing a project or running the completed service is a different stage.|Planning, building and operation sequence.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Is this about planning the centre, creating the building, or using it?|

067|The entrance faces the street but is one floor above it.|The entrance is reached from the street through a deep staircase.|At street level means at the height of the road surface. Facing the street does not establish the same elevation.|Elevation versus orientation/access route.|none||

068|The gardener described only the equipment needed.|The gardener stated only the desired planting result.|A technique is a way of carrying out a task. Tools and goals may support a technique but are not the method itself.|Method versus tools and outcome.|none||

069|They would bore below the surface without opening it.|They would excavate from above and leave the finished tunnel uncovered.|Cut and cover involves opening a trench and later covering the built tunnel. Both parts of the name describe the construction sequence.|Plausible tunnel methods; preserve technical definition.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|technical terminology: teacher review recommended|Think about what the two verbs in the technique's name suggest.|

070|They dug a broad shallow basin for collecting water.|They drilled a narrow vertical hole into the ground.|A trench is a long, narrow excavation. A basin spreads out broadly; a borehole goes mainly downwards.|Shape-based spatial distractors.|none||

071|It has permanently moved its services into the hall.|It plans to use the hall in the future but has not started yet.|Temporarily means for a limited time. A repeated activity can still be temporary, but the word does not imply permanent use.|Duration versus permanent/indefinite arrangement.|none||

072|They delay work on the ceiling rather than carry its weight.|They keep people away without supporting the structure.|Hold up here means physically support. The props carry the ceiling's weight; the delay sense is not intended.|Source physical-support sense of phrasal verb.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|What job do props perform when a ceiling has been damaged?|

073|A short decorative strip of wood covers the roof joint.|A wooden panel forms the wall beside the doorway.|A timber beam is a long structural wooden member. The sentence specifies a load-bearing role, rather than decoration or wall covering.|Structural role and material.|technical building term: teacher review recommended||

074|A straight brick wall closes off the entrance.|A flat brick path runs through the entrance.|An arch is a curved structure spanning an opening. Brick specifies its material; a wall or path lacks the stated curved spanning form.|Geometry and material in compound noun.|technical building term: teacher review recommended||

075|The worker mixed sand throughout the material underneath.|The worker made several separate heaps of sand around the edge.|A layer is a thickness of material spread over a surface. Mixing it throughout, or making isolated heaps, is different.|Distribution over a surface.|none||

076|They repaired a few fittings while leaving the building otherwise unchanged.|They built an unrelated hall in another town.|Rebuild means build again, usually after damage or destruction. The prefix re- signals repetition of the building process.|Re- form and restoration after damage.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Notice the prefix re- and the earlier storm damage. How do they connect?|

077|A maintenance procedure began while ferry services remained stopped.|The ferry's management structure changed without the service restarting.|In normal operation means functioning as a service. Here operation is not surgery, a repair procedure or management structure.|Intended service-functioning sense.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|What changed for people wanting to use the ferry after repairs?|

078|The existing railway would run more frequent trains over the same length of track.|The villages would receive a separate railway unrelated to the existing line.|An extension adds to an existing line or system. A more frequent timetable alone would not extend its physical reach.|Physical addition versus service frequency.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Look at which places the line would reach after the work.|

079|Only the manager can recommend the purchase without approving it.|Only the manager can process payment after someone else approves it.|Authorise means give official permission. Recommending a purchase or handling payment is not necessarily authorising it.|Authority versus recommendation/payment.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Consider the manager's role before the purchase can go ahead.|

080|It restored an unpowered passenger carriage pulled by a separate engine.|It restored a train engine driven by an electric motor.|A steam locomotive is the engine that moves a train using steam power. It is neither an unpowered coach nor an electric engine.|Same railway domain with source power distinction.|technical railway term: teacher review recommended||

081|The equipment stores hot water without producing steam.|The equipment cools steam back into water.|A boiler heats water; in this steam-engine context it supplies steam. This differs from a tank that merely stores hot water or a condenser that cools vapour.|Keep source steam context; avoid claiming every domestic boiler makes steam.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym; definition-like context replaced with a natural scenario|technical sense: not all boilers are steam generators|Think about what a steam engine needs before it can run.|A fault in the boiler stopped the steam engine from running.

082|It will explain the new system to staff but keep the old one in use.|It will remove the new system from service next month.|Introduce a system here means begin using it. Introducing a topic or explaining a system is a different sense of the verb.|Implementation versus explanation/removal.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Consider what will change next month, rather than what staff are told about it.|

083|Classrooms will be designed to allow filters to be added later.|Existing filters will be inspected without installing any equipment.|Be fitted with means have equipment installed. A design allowance or an inspection is not an installation.|Installed versus compatible/inspected.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Is the sentence describing the equipment the rooms will have, or just a design possibility?|

084|The water will change from liquid into vapour.|The vapour will be removed without changing its physical state.|Condense means change from gas to liquid. On cold glass, water vapour forms liquid droplets; evaporation goes the other way.|Direction of phase change.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Consider what can appear on the surface of a cold glass.|

085|They let fine dry paint particles leave the room.|They let ordinary warm air leave, without any paint vapour.|Fumes are strong gases or vapours, often unpleasant or harmful. Paint dust is solid particulate matter rather than vapour.|Vapour versus dust; avoid exaggerating toxicity.|health wording: strong fumes are not all equally toxic||

086|A drain removes water from the underground room.|A service passage carries people but has no airflow function.|Ventilation concerns the movement of air. A ventilation shaft is a passage serving that airflow, rather than a drain or ordinary access passage.|Airflow function distinct from adjacent tunnel uses.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym; definition-like context replaced with a natural scenario|technical building term: teacher review recommended|Think about the purpose of the passage, rather than just its location underground.|The maintenance crew cleared a blockage in the ventilation shaft beneath the theatre.

087|The route was longer even though traffic moved freely.|A vehicle breakdown delayed only the speaker's car.|Congestion means an excessive build-up of traffic that impedes movement. Not every delay is caused by congestion.|Cause of delay rather than delay alone.|none||

088|The route is a one-way path ending at a different destination.|The route consists of several unconnected paths.|A circuit is a route that goes around and returns to its starting point. It need not be a perfect circle.|Loop without overclaiming circular geometry.|none||

089|Cycling is a required replacement, with no choice allowed.|Cycling is an extra activity that must be done as well as taking the bus.|An alternative is another possible choice. It is not necessarily compulsory or an additional task that must also be done.|Choice versus obligation/addition.|none||

090|The area is open and spacious but access is restricted by a gate.|The area is underground but forms a wide, open hall with plenty of room.|A confined space is physically enclosed and limited in room. Restricted permission alone does not describe its physical size or enclosure.|Source everyday sense; avoid legal workplace classification.|technical safety term: everyday meaning, not a legal definition||

091|It needs radios with extra features even if they sometimes fail.|It needs radios that work only under ideal conditions.|Reliable means dependable: the team can count on the radios to work consistently. Features alone do not establish reliability.|Dependability versus features/conditional operation.|none||

092|A steam-powered mechanism moves it.|A manual winding mechanism moves it.|An electric motor turns electrical energy into movement. Other power sources may move a lift, but they are not electric motors.|Mechanical function and electrical input.|technical device term: teacher review recommended||

093|The boat is the destination to which supplies are sent.|The boat is the cause of a shortage rather than the delivery method.|By means of introduces the method used to do something. The boat is how supplies arrive, not their destination.|Instrument/method versus cause/destination.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|What role does the boat play in getting the supplies to the island?|

094|It can store energy at the battery without delivering it to the lamp.|It can convert energy into light inside the lamp rather than transmit it between devices.|Transfer power means transmit energy from one part of a system to another. Storage and generation are different functions.|Energy transmission versus storage/generation.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|technical wording: power/energy distinction for source-level paraphrase|Compare what happens between the devices with what happens inside a device.|

095|A battery stored electricity produced earlier.|A transformer changed voltage without producing electricity.|A generator produces electrical power. A battery stores energy, while a transformer changes electrical voltage.|Plausible device-level distractors.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|technical device term: teacher review recommended|What kind of equipment could keep the lights running during an outage?|

096|It proposed an electric railway in a shallow trench near the surface.|It proposed a deep tunnel railway powered by steam.|Deep-level specifies a location well below ground, and electric specifies the power source. Both details belong to this compound expression.|Test both location and traction source.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|technical railway terminology: teacher review recommended|Check both parts of the railway description before choosing.|

097|The six panels are optional equipment supplied alongside the display.|The display is used to manufacture six panels.|Be made up of introduces the parts composing a whole. It does not mean that those parts are merely optional accessories or products.|Composition versus accessory/product.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Consider how the six panels relate to the complete display.|

098|The doorway was low, but its width was not limited.|The doorway was far from the delivery entrance.|Narrow refers to limited width. Low describes height, so a low doorway is not necessarily narrow.|Width versus height/distance.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Which physical dimension would affect whether the furniture could pass through?|

099|It interrupted the building's internet connection.|It interrupted only the control signal while electrical energy remained available.|Power supply refers to the provision of electrical energy. A cable can carry other kinds of signals, but those are not the intended sense.|Power versus data/control signals.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|What service to the building depends on this cable in the sentence?|

100|It was described as a commercial success regardless of its engineering.|It was described as an ambitious plan that had not yet worked.|A technical achievement is something successfully accomplished through technology or engineering. Profitability or ambition alone does not establish that accomplishment.|Technical success versus commercial success/intention.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Which aspect of the spacecraft is being praised?|

101|It hopes to increase sales even if costs increase by more.|It hopes to earn exactly enough to cover its costs.|Make a profit means income exceeds costs. Higher sales alone may not produce profit, and covering costs exactly is breaking even.|Profit versus revenue and break-even.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Sales and costs both matter here. What comparison would show the bakery's result?|

102|The procedure has been proposed but is not yet being used.|The procedure has been written down but implementation is postponed.|In place here means established and operating. Having a proposal or document alone is not enough.|Operational status versus documentation/intention.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Is the writer describing an idea still being discussed or an arrangement already being used?|

103|The workshop began at exactly the same time as the talk.|The workshop began after a long interval.|Soon afterwards combines sequence with a short time gap. It does not mean simultaneous events or a much later occasion.|Timing: after and soon both matter.; hint revised to a contextual cue without a defining synonym|none|Compare when the two events began.|
